title: Pipe operator (`|>`)
summary: PHP 8.5 adds a pipe operator: `$value |> callable` invokes `callable` with `$value` as its only argument, so a chain of single-argument transformations can be written left-to-right instead of nesting function calls.
new_code_policy: On a feature ceiling of 8.5 or above, prefer a `|>` pipe chain over deeply nested single-argument function calls when the value being transformed is the only thing changing from step to step; pair it with first-class callable syntax (`strtoupper(...)`) rather than wrapping each step in a closure.
existing_code_policy: Do not bulk-convert nested function calls to pipe chains. Nesting and piping are only equivalent when every intermediate call takes exactly the piped value as its sole argument; a call that also needs extra arguments (e.g. `array_map($fn, $list)`) requires wrapping in a closure or first-class-callable partial before it can sit in a chain, which changes the line rather than merely reordering it. Migrate a call chain only where it is already being touched for another reason and the rewrite is a clear readability win.
guideline: Prefer `$value |> f(...) |> g(...)` over `g(f($value))` once the feature ceiling reaches PHP 8.5, for chains of single-argument transformations.
details: PHP 8.5 added the pipe (`|>`) operator (RFC pipe-operator-v3): `$value |> $callable` calls `$callable` with `$value` as its sole argument, and the operator is left-associative, so `$value |> f(...) |> g(...)` evaluates as `g(f($value))` but reads top-to-bottom in the order the transformations happen. This is purely additive syntax; it introduces no new runtime semantics beyond ordinary function invocation and changes no existing construct. No PHP 8.2, 8.3 or 8.4 UPGRADING file mentions a pipe operator (the only pre-8.5 hits are unrelated: the `POSIX_PC_PIPE_BUF` constant in 8.3 and the `SO_NOSIGPIPE` constant in 8.4), and no later UPGRADING file records a deprecation or removal.
